rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source alone. I did not request implementation source. I found no adequacy gap.

**Indexing obligations.** `Index<Span> for str` must behave like `&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and UTF-8 boundary checks. The test `span_indexes_str_at_utf8_byte_boundaries` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` covers this. Its source is `"aé🦀"`, which is 7 bytes: `a` is 1 byte, `é` is 2 and `🦀` is 4.
- **Valid spans:** `Span::new(1, 3)` yields `"é"`. `Span::new(7, 7)` yields `""`, so an empty span at `len` is accepted and `end` is exclusive.
- **Panic cases:** each of these is asserted to panic through `catch_unwind`.
  - `Span::new(2, 3)` has a start inside `é`.
  - `Span::new(0, 2)` has an end inside `é`.
  - `Span::new(2, 2)` is an empty span on a non-boundary.
  - `Span::new(0, 8)` has `end` greater than `len`.
  - `Span::new(3, 1)` has `start` greater than `end`.
- **Construction:** `Span::new` is called outside the `catch_unwind` closure. So the test also shows that `new` does not validate or panic, and that an invalid span can be constructed.

**Offsets from the original snapshot, including nested items.**
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` checks byte-based spans on multibyte text. The expected spans are `Span::new(0, source.len())`, `Span::new(0, 2)` and `Span::new(6, 10)`. It also asserts `&source[item.span]` equals the selected text.
- `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` covers nested items inside a directive, a quote and a list. It asserts `item.span.start` and `item.name_span` equal offsets in the original source. It also asserts `selected.text() == &source[item.span]`. This supports "from the start of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item".

**Type shape and trait implementations.**
- The public `start` and `end` fields are read directly in the setext test.
- `Span::new` is used throughout.
- `Copy` is exercised because the `catch_unwind` closure uses `span` after it is iterated.
- `PartialEq` and `Debug` are exercised by `assert_eq!` on `Span` values.
- `Clone` is implied by the `Copy` bound.
- `Eq` is a marker trait with no behavior of its own.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` is a compile-time attribute with no runtime conditional. The `public_exports_match_the_appendix` test in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs` also checks the public inventory.

All the observable obligations are tested with assertions that match the requirement.

text: `trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
